task: Publish earned points from D1 after queued audit finalization and display available scores with coverage.
state: Implemented and verified locally on codex/publish-earned-score, based on merge commit 93515416ce67345a89f1137f0f96c7391afb8615. No production changes.
decisions: Finalization sums measured component.points already stored in D1; the front end consumes the resulting score using the existing report API and polling.

New queued reports mark the score as earned_points. A stored verified zero is numeric. No measured components means a null score and the UI shows No checks measured. Retrieval failure keeps its unable_to_assess state with no report.

Preserve historical reports and in-flight drafts without the marker, and preserve rubric-level redistribution for evidenced exclusions. Display totals to two decimal places with fixed pillar maxima of 40 and 60.
constraints: Preserve the 60-second model timeout, the 1,000 ms Worker CPU cap, and the existing usage guards and limits.
Do not deploy, make production changes, invoke the live model, or commit merchant data.
completed: Native local workerd and D1 replay used a hash-verified saved Faherty capture, saved public supporting resources, and a deterministic model response. D1 stored 39 components and the existing queue published 38 total, 4 Structure, and 34 Content with 4 of 24 checks fully measured and incomplete status.
Local Chrome rendered the three Faherty scores and published coverage from the actual local API response, with browser traffic intercepted. It stopped polling after the terminal response.

Queue and display fixtures cover measured zero, no measured components, retrieval failure, the configured model timeout, incomplete coverage with component points, and a complete report with an evidenced exclusion.

Independent Terra review confirmed D1/API behavior and identified test and presentation refinements. Final review confirmed the complete exclusion fixture and score display changes, with no remaining blocker.
remaining: Production rollout requires separate authorization. Existing cached reports retain their original interpretation.
Real model behavior and wider Faherty check coverage are outside this change.
